flawed_step: Line 0678 (Appendix, proof of Lemma \ref{taylor}(iii)): "But from a change of variables we have $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^0 \exp(-(\alpha-t)^2/2)\,dt = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\erf(-\sqrt{2}\alpha)$" -- the evaluation of the Gaussian integral is wrong; the correct value is $\frac12 + \frac12\erf(-\alpha/\sqrt{2})$. This propagates to the target identity at line 0672, the statement of Lemma \ref{taylor}(iii) at line 0626, and Corollary (iv) at line 0710.
counterexample: Take alpha = 1 (a legitimate fixed value in the lemma). With erf defined as in line 0610, erf(z) = (2/sqrt(pi)) int_0^z e^{-t^2} dt, the left-hand side of line 0678 is (1/sqrt(2pi)) int_{-infty}^0 e^{-(1-t)^2/2} dt = Phi(-1) = 0.158655..., where Phi is the standard normal CDF (substitute s = (t-1)/sqrt(2)). The right-hand side as written is 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-sqrt(2)) = 1/2 - (1/2)(0.954500...) = 0.022750.... These differ. The correct closed form is 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-1/sqrt(2)) = 1/2 - (1/2)(0.682689...) = 0.158655..., i.e. the error-function argument must be alpha/sqrt(2), not sqrt(2)*alpha. Consistency check on the lemma itself: e^{-z} sum_{j<n} z^j/j! = P(Poisson(z) <= n-1) with z = n + alpha*sqrt(n), which by the CLT tends to Phi(-alpha) = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-alpha/sqrt(2)), confirming the stated constant is off by a factor of 2 inside erf.
